text: Ten fictional nonprofit programme passages, each with one quote of every variant type for citation-checker testing.

passages.source_passage: In the Marrowfield district, the Tessaly Access Trust estimates that 4,200 residents live with a mobility, visual or hearing impairment. A 2022 household survey found that only 18% of these residents owned an assistive device suited to their needs. Most health posts do not stock wheelchairs, hearing aids or white canes, and repair services are almost non-existent. Families often travel more than sixty kilometres to the regional hospital in Dunmere, where waiting lists exceed nine months. Local schools have no ramps or accessible latrines, so many children with disabilities are forced to leave education early. This proposal builds on a pilot in which trained technicians fitted 310 devices and adapted twelve public buildings.

passages.source_passage: Before each distribution day, volunteers should review the household register with their team leader. Each household receives one long-lasting insecticidal net for every two sleeping people, up to a maximum of four nets. Do not hand out nets to anyone whose name is missing from the register; instead, refer them to the supervisor at the registration table. Show families how to hang the net over the sleeping mat and tuck the edges under the mattress. Remind them that nets should be aired in the shade for 24 hours before first use. In the 2021 campaign around Lake Odessi, volunteers reached 92% of registered households within three weeks.

passages.source_passage: During the 2023 programme year, the Brightwater Evening Learning Network ran 46 literacy circles across the villages of Kessa and Lomari. A total of 1,130 adults enrolled, of whom roughly two thirds were women. Learners met three evenings a week in schoolrooms lent by local headteachers. By the final assessment in December, 61% of learners could read a short newspaper paragraph aloud and write a simple letter. Attendance dipped during the harvest months, and nine circles did not reopen after the October break. Facilitators reported that solar lamps funded by your grant allowed classes to continue after dark. We have not yet secured materials for the advanced reading level requested by graduates.

passages.source_passage: In 2023 the Corvan Skills Centre in Ndaleni trained 284 young people aged 18 to 24 in welding, tailoring, solar installation and catering. Courses lasted six months and combined classroom sessions with a placement at a local business. Of the graduates, 71% were in paid work or self-employment three months after completing their course. Women made up 40% of enrolments, although no women enrolled in the welding course despite targeted outreach. The centre did not meet its target of 300 trainees because a fire closed the catering kitchen for seven weeks. With the funder's support, twenty-two employers have now signed agreements to host apprentices next year.

passages.source_passage: The mid-term evaluation of the Harrowdale Cash for Food programme covered 1,850 households enrolled between March 2022 and June 2023. Each household received a monthly transfer of 45 dollars through mobile money. Households reporting two or more meals a day rose from 38% at baseline to 67% at mid-term. Evaluators found no evidence that transfers raised prices in local markets. However, one in five recipients said payments were often delayed by more than ten days, and older recipients in remote hamlets struggled to use the mobile platform. The evaluation team recommends adding cash-out agents in the three most isolated wards. Payments were not linked to any work requirement.

passages.source_passage: This update covers the first term of the 2024 school year in the Kanté and Sorobi districts. The Nourish Ahead programme now serves a hot lunch to 9,600 pupils in 32 primary schools, up from 7,100 pupils last year. Meals combine millet, cowpeas and fortified oil, and parent committees run the kitchens on a rotating basis. Average attendance in participating schools reached 88%, compared with 74% in neighbouring schools without meals. Two schools did not receive deliveries for eleven days in October because the access road flooded. The board is asked to approve a buffer stock of one month's supplies at the district warehouse. No cases of food contamination have been reported this term.

passages.source_passage: Since 2019, the Umlazi Ridge Care Collective has trained 140 community caregivers to visit people living with HIV in their homes. Each caregiver supports around eight clients, checking medication adherence, dressing wounds and helping families plan meals. In the catchment area of roughly 60,000 people, the nearest clinic is a ninety-minute walk for many households. Clients who are bedridden cannot collect their own antiretroviral refills, and before the programme many simply went without treatment. An internal review in 2023 found that 83% of visited clients had an undetectable viral load. Caregivers are not paid a salary and currently rely on a small travel stipend that does not cover rising transport costs.

passages.source_passage: Between January and June 2024, the Fairhold Paralegal Service opened 512 new cases across its five outreach points in the Teller Valley. Land and inheritance disputes made up 46% of cases, followed by domestic violence and unpaid wages. Paralegals resolved 290 cases through mediation without going to court. Twenty-three cases were referred to partner lawyers, but only nine of these have been heard so far because the magistrate's court sat for just four weeks. The board should note that the service did not open its planned sixth outreach point in Wendi, as no suitable premises were available. Client feedback remains positive, with most clients saying they would recommend the service to a neighbour.

passages.source_passage: Each playgroup session runs for two hours and should include free play, a story circle and a shared snack. Groups work best with no more than 15 children and at least two volunteers present. Never leave children unattended, even for a few minutes, and do not use phones during sessions. Encourage caregivers to stay and join in, because children learn more when a familiar adult plays alongside them. At the end of each month, record attendance and any developmental concerns in the green logbook. In our 2023 pilot across the Pellow hill villages, three quarters of regular attenders showed gains in early language skills.

passages.source_passage: This monitoring report covers the quarter ending 30 September 2024 for the Saltmere Coast Early Warning Programme. Volunteers tested all 27 village sirens, and 24 were working correctly; the remaining three are awaiting replacement batteries. SMS alerts reached 11,400 registered phone numbers within an average of six minutes during the August drill. However, the drill showed that evacuation routes in Port Lissan were not clearly marked, and several families did not know their assigned shelter. Shelter managers in all nine coastal wards have now trained village volunteers in first aid. No storm warnings were issued during the quarter, so the system has not yet been tested in a real event.
